error.propagation:elements: These elements do not give a position on the orbit. For a hyperbola, the true anomaly must be between the two asymptotes.
error.propagation:center: The application has no data for the center at the start time. Select a different center in the top bar.

flight.label: Top view of the flight relative to {center}
flight.caption: View from the +Z axis of the frame ({frame}). Center: {center}. A square shows the start. A diamond shows a maneuver. A circle shows a closest approach with its date ({scale}). The thin lines are the paths of the bodies during the flight.
flight.reference: The dashed line is the trajectory from the file.
flight.now: The ring shows the spacecraft at the time of the view.

diff.label: Position difference from the flight on the screen for each comparison flight
diff.axisX: Time after the start of the flight (d)

propagation.title: Propagation
propagation.intro: This screen shows the start state and the force model of the flight. The engine integrates the equations of motion with all forces of the model in each step.
propagation.noMission: No mission is open. Set a start state and a force model, then calculate the flight. The application makes a mission that has only this flight.
propagation.noFlight: This mission has no flight. Calculate the flight from the plan first.
propagation.contextNote: The values are relative to {center}, in the frame {frame}. Change the center and the frame in the top bar: the state of the spacecraft stays the same.
propagation.elementsNeedBody: Orbit elements are not available for the solar system barycenter. Select a body as the center in the top bar.
propagation.elementsNote: Two-body elements of the state relative to {center}. The reference plane of the angles is the XY plane of the frame.
propagation.example: Set example values for an orbit about {center}
propagation.exampleNote: The values in the fields are example values. Change them to the values of your spacecraft.
propagation.copyNow: Use the state of the flight at the time of the view
propagation.outside: Maneuvers that are not between the start and the end: {n}. The application removes them when you apply the changes.
propagation.manualNote: You changed the start state or the force model of this flight. A new flight calculation from the plan replaces your changes.
propagation.anchorNote: A change of the start state or of the force model moves the path at each maneuver. The maneuvers keep their values, thus the flight can miss its encounters. Use the targeter on the Maneuvers screen to aim them again.
propagation.needBody: The model must have the gravity of one body or more.
propagation.moonsHint: The moons of Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto pull the spacecraft as separate masses. If this is off, each planet and its moons are one mass at their barycenter.
propagation.j2Hint: The engine applies the J2 term inside 300 radii of each planet.
propagation.srpHint: Cannonball model: a sphere with one area and one reflectivity coefficient. The mass stays constant.
propagation.asteroidNote: The engine has data for Ceres, Vesta and Psyche from 1980 to 2060. Outside this range, their gravity is off.
propagation.notModeled: Not in the model: engine burns with a duration, forces that depend on the attitude, atmospheric drag, and gravity harmonics above J2.
propagation.now: State of the spacecraft at the time of the view
propagation.study: Effect of each force on this flight
propagation.studyIntro: The application propagates the flight again with one change of the force model for each row. Each value is the distance between that flight and the flight on the screen at the same time. Thus you can see which forces are important for this flight.
propagation.studyDirty: Apply or discard the changes before you do the comparison.
propagation.studyOld: The flight changed after the last comparison.
propagation.stopped: The comparison flight stopped before this time
propagation.stoppedHit: The comparison flight hit the surface of {body} at {time} {scale} and stopped.
propagation.studyNote: The columns with a body show the position difference at that closest approach. Select a row to show or hide its line in the graph.
propagation.toleranceIntro: The application propagates the flight again with larger relative tolerances. The flight on the screen uses the tolerance 1 × 10⁻¹³. The difference between the tolerance 1 × 10⁻¹² and the flight on the screen is an estimate of the numerical error of this flight.
propagation.toleranceNote: The estimate includes the error of the integration only. It does not include the errors of the ephemeris data and of the force model: refer to the Accuracy screen.
propagation.modeArcNote: Each comparison flight starts again from the state of the flight on the screen after each maneuver. A value thus shows the effect of the force in one arc of the flight.
propagation.modeWholeNote: Each comparison flight has the same start state and the same maneuvers as the flight on the screen. Each flyby makes a difference larger, thus the values after some flybys are very large.
propagation.studyNoteArc: A flyby makes a small difference much larger: the largest difference is usually at the end of an arc, after the flyby.
propagation.studyNoteWhole: The comparison flights do not use the stored states of the solver at the maneuvers.
propagation.toleranceWhole: With one start only, the values show how sensitive the flight is: a flight through some flybys with fixed maneuvers does not have one stable end.
